title: Comparison of quotient chart morphisms on an intersection
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible $X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $S$ its graded section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. Let $d,e>0$, $s\in S_d$, $t\in S_e$, and opens $U,V\subseteq X$ with underlying sets respectively the nonvanishing loci of $s,t$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Suppose given morphisms $g:U\to\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ and $h:V\to\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. For each of these morphisms $k$, assume that for every positive-degree homogeneous $a\in S_r$, every $n\geq0$, and every $\xi\in S_{nr}$, on the ambient image $W$ of $k^{-1}(D_+(a))$ its scalar pullback satisfies $k^\sharp(\xi/a^n)\cdot(a^n)|_W=\xi|_W$. Then $g|_{U\cap V}=h|_{U\cap V}$ as morphisms to $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$. This comparison asserts no existence of morphisms.

proof.text: Apply sectionRing_overlap_base_map to the original quotient-chart hypotheses to identify the underlying maps of the two restrictions.
Apply sectionRing_overlap_sheaf_map with this identification to obtain equality of every sheaf component, transported along the equality of inverse images.

Combine the base equality and transported component equalities using Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ext. This is a decomposition into the continuous-map and sheaf-map components of a scheme morphism.
